description: Alpine updates. (1) apk pins (custom.alpine CDN datasource): ALL non-major apk bumps (patch/pin/digest/minor) share ONE 'alpine packages' group so they open a single mutually-buildable PR — Alpine repos keep only the latest build of each apk and purge older ones from the index, so a Dockerfile pinning a drifted version fails to build; splitting apk bumps across PRs deadlocks (each PR still pins the purged versions the other bumps). No soak, run any time, and automerged once CI (the real Docker build — the exact check a stale pin would fail) passes. separateMinorPatch/separateMajorMinor are forced false for the custom.alpine datasource so no apk bump ever splits onto its own branch. (2) Alpine base image (docker datasource): minor bumps cross release lines and require hand-editing the consumer's depNameTemplate (alpine_X_Y/) — which now also drives the CDN registry URL — so they are gated to manual review; patch base bumps stay in-line and automerge via docker.json's bundle. (3) a TRANSITIONAL hostRules throttle for repology.org, retained ONLY until every consumer has migrated off the repology datasource — delete it then (see that rule's description). (4) node image bumps (minor/patch) are gated to manual review: node:*-alpine carries an Alpine release line that nothing else gates. Extend AFTER automerge.json and docker.json. Major bumps fall through to default.json's manual-review rule.

alpine.description: Alpine apk versions, read from the distro's own package index on dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org — the same host apk installs from. format 'html' turns every href in the directory listing into a version candidate; the consumer's extractVersionTemplate picks the one belonging to each package. The registry URL is DERIVED from the alpine_X_Y/ prefix in the consumer's depNameTemplate, so the Alpine release line stays a single-place edit in the consumer and this preset stays version-agnostic — do NOT hardcode a release line here. The datasource name 'alpine' is load-bearing: every apk packageRule below matches on 'custom.alpine', so a consumer naming it anything else silently drops out of every Alpine rule. /main/ and /x86_64/ are fleet-wide constants. Community packages need a consumer-side registryUrls override: custom datasources use registryStrategy 'first', so the override REPLACES this URL rather than adding to it — listing both warns 'Excess registryUrls found for datasource lookup' and uses only the first. x86_64 assumes no cross-arch version skew (none measured across x86_64/aarch64/armv7); multi-arch CI catches a builder lag. A package pointed at the WRONG index is SILENTLY untracked: the index fetch succeeds, no href matches extractVersion, and Renovate reports no updates, no warning and no dashboard entry — so verify a new pin's index before adding it.

hostRules.description: Throttle Renovate's HTTP traffic to repology.org, the datasource behind every apk pin. Repology rate-limits aggressively and Mend-hosted Renovate runs from shared IPs, so unthrottled bursts get 429/5xx-ed and surface as 'Repology lookup failed with unexpected error' + 'Failed to look up repology package alpine_X_Y/<pkg>: no-result' on the Dependency Dashboard. That message is AMBIGUOUS: the repology datasource emits 'no-result' both when the package genuinely does not exist AND when the HTTP request failed — so it reads like a bad depNameTemplate or a typo'd package name when it is actually transport-layer throttling. Before chasing a config bug, curl https://repology.org/tools/project-by?repo=alpine_X_Y&name_type=binname&target_page=api_v1_project&noautoresolve=on&name=<pkg>; a 200 with the right payload means the config is fine and this throttle is the fix. abortOnError:false keeps a repology hiccup from killing the whole run (renovatebot/renovate#44329 made abortOnError actually respected for this datasource); the 60s timeout absorbs Repology's slow tail. This is NOT cosmetic: while lookups fail, Renovate cannot see apk drift, and since Alpine purges older builds of each apk the first signal becomes a red Docker build instead of a PR — the early-warning system goes dark. Do NOT raise maxRequestsPerSecond/concurrentRequestLimit to 'speed up' lookups; that re-triggers the rate limiting this exists to avoid. This throttle is also NOT a reason to keep repology forever: no first-class apk/Alpine datasource has SHIPPED yet, but renovatebot/renovate#40250 ('feat(datasource): add APK datasource support') is open and is the intended migration once released — at which point this hostRules entry, and the consumer-side repology customManager it protects, should be revisited together. TRANSITIONAL: as of 2026-08-19 the apk datasource is custom.alpine (see customDatasources above) and this entry exists ONLY for consumers that have not yet migrated their customManager off repology. Delete it once all of them have — see docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-19-alpine-custom-datasource-design.md, Phase 3.

packageRules.description: Keep every Alpine apk (custom.alpine) bump on ONE branch. default.json sets separateMajorMinor:true, and separateMinorPatch would prefix the groupSlug (patch-/major-) and split otherwise-grouped apk bumps onto separate branches. Because Alpine purges the old build of a package the moment it drifts, any apk pin left behind on a separate branch fails to build — so all apk update types must co-bump. Force both flags false for the whole custom.alpine datasource (NOT scoped by matchUpdateTypes — a major update wouldn't match that filter and would keep default.json's split). Do NOT re-split apk updates by update type.

Alpine apk (custom.alpine) non-major pins (patch/pin/digest/minor): ONE group, skip the soak, run off-schedule, automerge. Formerly split into 'alpine packages' (patch/pin/digest, automerge) + 'alpine packages (minor)' (manual) — that opened two PRs in any window where one package drifted patch and another drifted minor, and BOTH failed CI because each still pinned the purged versions the other PR bumped. Deadlock. Unified into one group so every drifted apk pin co-bumps in a single PR that automerges once CI passes. Automerge is safe HERE precisely because unifying the group makes the PR self-consistent — CI runs the real Docker build, which is the exact check that would fail on a stale pin. Do NOT re-split by update type to isolate minor bumps for review — that re-introduces the deadlock.

Node runtime images carry an Alpine release line (node:24.19.0-alpine is Alpine 3.24.1), and Node moves that base at its own cadence — including on patch rebuilds. A crossing invalidates the consumer's alpine_X_Y/ depNameTemplate AND, because this preset derives the CDN registry URL from that prefix, its registry URL too. Gate every node image bump to manual review so a human checks the resulting line. Deliberately sets NO groupName: node.json's toolchain-versions group must keep node and pnpm co-bumping in ONE PR, and a group here would split them — the gate still works because a single automerge:false upgrade disables the whole branch and addLabels is unioned across upgrades. Majors already carry needs-review via docker.json's runtime rule. digest/pinDigest are EXCLUDED — a known, accepted gap: a same-tag rebuild can re-point the floating node:*-alpine alias at a new Alpine line. Pinning node:X-alpine3.24 instead was REJECTED: Renovate cannot couple the node version and the Alpine suffix, so an explicit suffix would freeze the line with nothing ever signalling the move to 3.25 — trading a rare silent crossing for a permanent silent stall. Gating digests was rejected on automerge cost (pinDigests is on, so digest refreshes are frequent). This rule is UNCONDITIONAL for every :alpine consumer, and is the THIRD place node/docker.io/library/node is named across these presets — keep it in sync with node.json's toolchain-versions and docker.json's dockerfile-bases negation list.

Alpine base image (docker datasource) minor bumps cross release lines, which requires hand-editing the consumer's depNameTemplate (alpine_X_Y/) — now also the source of the CDN registry URL. Gate ONLY these to manual review; never automerge. Patch bumps and digest-only rebuilds stay in-line (template still valid) and ride docker.json's 'dockerfile bases' group + automerge.json's non-major bundle.
